messages.What it is: Your pupils responded unusually to light and this needs further checks.
messages.What you can do: Attend eye or neurology follow-up as advised.
messages.When to get help: Seek urgent help for sudden vision loss, severe headache or weakness.

messages.What it is: An abnormal reflex was found on examination and may need further tests.
messages.What you can do: Attend follow-up tests as advised.
messages.When to get help: Seek help for new weakness, numbness or difficulty walking.

messages.What it is: Dark velvety skin on the neck or armpits is a sign your body is resisting insulin.
messages.What you can do: Losing weight, cutting sugar and daily exercise can fade it and lower diabetes risk.
messages.When to get help: Ask your doctor for a diabetes test if you have not had one.

messages.What it is: Acid reflux is stomach acid rising into the food pipe, causing heartburn. Diet and tablets help.
messages.What you can do: Eat smaller meals, avoid late eating, spicy and oily food, and raise the head of your bed.
messages.When to get help: See a doctor for difficulty swallowing, vomiting blood, black stools or weight loss.

messages.What it is: A heart attack means part of the heart muscle was starved of blood. Treatment now prevents another.
messages.What you can do: Take every tablet, rest as advised, stop smoking and attend cardiac follow-up.
messages.When to get help: Call emergency help immediately for chest pain or breathlessness.

messages.What it is: Your heart recently had a reduced blood supply. Recovery needs rest, medicines and follow-up.
messages.What you can do: Take all tablets, attend cardiac follow-up, stop smoking and build up activity gradually.
messages.When to get help: Call emergency services for chest pain, breathlessness or fainting.

messages.What it is: Your kidneys were suddenly affected, often by dehydration, infection or medicines.
messages.What you can do: Drink fluids as advised and pause any tablets your doctor has told you to stop while unwell.
messages.When to get help: Seek help urgently if urine output drops, or for vomiting, confusion or swelling.

messages.What it is: After a shocking event, strong feelings are normal and usually fade within weeks.
messages.What you can do: Keep routines, sleep, talk to people you trust and avoid alcohol.
messages.When to get help: Contact your clinic if symptoms last over a month. Call 1926 if in crisis.

messages.What it is: Alcohol dependence is a medical condition, not a weakness. Treatment and support work.
messages.What you can do: Do not stop suddenly on your own - ask your clinic about safe withdrawal and counselling.
messages.When to get help: Seek urgent help for shaking, confusion, seizures or seeing things when not drinking.

messages.What it is: Heavy drinking harms the liver, heart, blood pressure and mood. Cutting down helps quickly.
messages.What you can do: Set alcohol-free days, avoid drinking alone and ask your clinic about support.
messages.When to get help: Seek help if you shake, sweat or feel very anxious when not drinking - sudden stopping can be risky.

messages.What it is: Alcohol raises blood pressure, sugar and weight. Less is better for long-term conditions.
messages.What you can do: Keep to at most 2 drinks a day with alcohol-free days, and never drink with certain medicines.
messages.When to get help: Talk to your clinic if you find it hard to cut down.

messages.What it is: An allergic reaction is the body overreacting to a food, medicine or insect sting.
messages.What you can do: Avoid the trigger if known and take antihistamines as advised.
messages.When to get help: Seek urgent help for lip or throat swelling, wheeze or feeling faint.

messages.What it is: You have an allergy. Knowing and avoiding the trigger is the best protection.
messages.What you can do: Keep a list of your allergies and show it at every clinic and pharmacy visit.
messages.When to get help: Seek urgent help for swelling of lips or throat or difficulty breathing.

messages.What it is: Anaemia means low haemoglobin, so less oxygen is carried. It causes tiredness and breathlessness.
messages.What you can do: Eat iron-rich foods like green leaves, lentils, meat and eggs, and take iron tablets if prescribed.
messages.When to get help: See a doctor for breathlessness, chest pain, dizziness or black stools.

messages.What it is: Angina is chest pain from narrowed heart arteries, often on exertion. It warns of heart attack risk.
messages.What you can do: Take your heart tablets daily, keep GTN spray with you, stop smoking and walk regularly.
messages.When to get help: Call for help if pain lasts over 15 minutes or is not relieved by rest or GTN.

messages.What it is: Angioedema is deep swelling of lips, face or throat, from allergy or ACE inhibitor tablets.
messages.What you can do: Note any suspected medicine and tell your doctor. Never restart an ACE inhibitor after this.
messages.When to get help: Go to hospital at once for swelling of tongue or throat or difficulty breathing.

sourceNames: Acute ST elevation myocardial infarction of anterior wall

messages.What it is: You have had a serious heart attack affecting the front of the heart. Follow-up is essential.
messages.What you can do: Take all tablets daily, avoid smoking, and join cardiac rehabilitation if offered.
messages.When to get help: Call emergency help for chest pain, breathlessness, swelling or fainting.

messages.What it is: Anxiety is a common condition of worry and tension. Talking therapy and medicines both help.
messages.What you can do: Practise slow breathing, walk daily, cut caffeine and keep regular sleep.
messages.When to get help: Contact your clinic if anxiety stops you doing daily tasks. Call 1926 if in crisis.

messages.What it is: An anxiety attack is sudden intense fear with a racing heart. It passes and is not dangerous.
messages.What you can do: Breathe slowly - in for 4, out for 6 - and remind yourself it will pass in minutes.
messages.When to get help: See your clinic if attacks are frequent. Get urgent help if chest pain does not settle.

messages.What it is: An anxiety disorder means worry is frequent and hard to control. It responds well to treatment.
messages.What you can do: Take medicines as prescribed, practise breathing exercises and stay active.
messages.When to get help: Contact your clinic if worsening. Call 1926 if in crisis.

sourceNames: Anxiety disorder due to a general medical condition

messages.What it is: Long-term illness can trigger anxiety. Treating both improves your wellbeing.
messages.What you can do: Practise slow breathing, stay active and take medicines as prescribed.
messages.When to get help: Contact your clinic if anxiety is affecting your sleep or daily life.

messages.What it is: An AV fistula is a surgical join between artery and vein, often made for dialysis.
messages.What you can do: Keep the arm clean, avoid tight sleeves, and do not let anyone take blood pressure on that arm.
messages.When to get help: Get help if the fistula stops buzzing, bleeds, or the arm becomes red, hot or painful.

messages.What it is: Asthma narrows the airways. A daily preventer inhaler keeps it controlled.
messages.What you can do: Use your preventer every day, even when well, and carry your reliever. Avoid smoke and dust.
messages.When to get help: Seek urgent help if the reliever is not working, you cannot speak in sentences or lips turn blue.

messages.What it is: Atherosclerosis is fatty build-up in the arteries. It raises heart attack and stroke risk.
messages.What you can do: Statin and aspirin, if prescribed, plus no smoking, daily walking and less oil, slow it down.
messages.When to get help: Get urgent help for chest pain, weakness on one side or leg pain when walking.

messages.What it is: Atrial fibrillation is an irregular heartbeat that raises stroke risk. Treatment lowers that risk.
messages.What you can do: Take your blood thinner and heart-rate tablets daily. Limit alcohol and caffeine.
messages.When to get help: Get urgent help for weakness, slurred speech, chest pain or fainting.

messages.What it is: Atrial flutter is a fast, regular abnormal rhythm. It is treatable and raises stroke risk.
messages.What you can do: Take rhythm and blood-thinning tablets as prescribed and attend cardiology follow-up.
messages.When to get help: Get urgent help for chest pain, fainting, weakness or trouble speaking.

messages.What it is: Most back pain improves in weeks with movement. Bed rest makes it worse.
messages.What you can do: Keep moving, use heat and paracetamol, and gradually return to normal activities.
messages.When to get help: Seek urgent help for numbness between the legs, bladder or bowel problems, or leg weakness.

messages.What it is: Bipolar disorder causes swings between very high and very low mood. Daily medicines keep it stable.
messages.What you can do: Take mood stabilisers daily, keep regular sleep, avoid alcohol and attend all appointments.
messages.When to get help: Get urgent help for no sleep for days, racing thoughts, or thoughts of self-harm. Call 1926.

sourceNames: Bipolar I disorder, most recent episode (or current) depressed

messages.What it is: You are in a low phase of bipolar disorder. Treatment helps lift it safely.
messages.What you can do: Take medicines daily, keep routine and sleep, and stay in touch with people.
messages.When to get help: Call 1926 or Sumithrayo 011 2696666 for thoughts of self-harm.

sourceNames: Bipolar I disorder, most recent episode (or current) manic, mild

messages.What it is: You are in a mild high phase. Sticking to medicines and sleep prevents it escalating.
messages.What you can do: Take medicines daily, keep regular sleep, avoid alcohol and big decisions.
messages.When to get help: Get urgent help if you stop sleeping, spend recklessly or feel unstoppable.

messages.What it is: You are in a low phase of bipolar disorder. Treatment helps lift it safely.
messages.What you can do: Take medicines daily, keep routine and sleep, and stay in touch with people.
messages.When to get help: Call 1926 or Sumithrayo 011 2696666 for thoughts of self-harm.

sourceNames: Bipolar I disorder, most recent episode (or current) manic, moderate

messages.What it is: You are in a high phase. Treatment and sleep help bring your mood back to normal.
messages.What you can do: Take medicines daily, protect sleep, avoid alcohol and let family support you.
messages.When to get help: Get urgent help if you stop sleeping or put yourself at risk.

sourceNames: Severe depressed bipolar I disorder without psychotic features

messages.What it is: You are in a severe low phase. Close treatment and support are needed now.
messages.What you can do: Take all medicines, keep every appointment and let family help you stay safe.
messages.When to get help: Go to hospital or call 1926 now for thoughts of self-harm.

patientFacingName: Bipolar disorder, severe depression with psychosis
sourceNames: Severe depressed bipolar I disorder with psychotic features

messages.What it is: You are in a severe low phase. Close treatment and support are needed now.
messages.What you can do: Take all medicines, keep every appointment and let family help you stay safe.
messages.When to get help: Go to hospital or call 1926 now for thoughts of self-harm or confusing thoughts.

sourceNames: Bipolar I disorder, most recent episode manic, without psychotic features, severe

messages.What it is: You are in a severe high phase. Close treatment and support are needed now.
messages.What you can do: Take all medicines and keep every appointment. Let family help you stay safe.
messages.When to get help: Go to hospital or call 1926 if you cannot sleep, feel out of control or at risk.

messages.What it is: Bipolar II causes low moods and milder highs. Medicines and routine keep it stable.
messages.What you can do: Take medicines daily, keep regular sleep and note early signs of mood change.
messages.When to get help: Contact your clinic if mood changes. Call 1926 for thoughts of self-harm.

messages.What it is: A bladder stone can cause pain, infection and difficulty passing urine.
messages.What you can do: Drink plenty of water and do not delay passing urine.
messages.When to get help: See a doctor for pain, blood in urine, or if you cannot empty your bladder.

messages.What it is: The bowel's blood supply was reduced. This needs hospital care and follow-up.
messages.What you can do: Take medicines as prescribed, stop smoking and attend all follow-up.
messages.When to get help: Seek urgent help for severe tummy pain, bloody stools or vomiting.

messages.What it is: Getting breathless on exertion may reflect the heart, lungs, weight or fitness.
messages.What you can do: Build activity up slowly, stop smoking and take heart or lung medicines as prescribed.
messages.When to get help: See a doctor if it is getting worse or comes with chest pain or ankle swelling.

messages.What it is: You have reacted to a calcium channel blocker (e.g. amlodipine). Other pressure tablets can be used.
messages.What you can do: Tell every doctor and pharmacist. Keep a note of the drug name with you.
messages.When to get help: Seek urgent help for swelling of lips or face or difficulty breathing.

messages.What it is: You are under care for cancer. Your treatment team will guide each step.
messages.What you can do: Attend every appointment, eat well, rest and ask questions when unsure.
messages.When to get help: Contact your team urgently for fever during chemotherapy, bleeding or severe pain.

messages.What it is: Chest pain from the heart means the heart muscle is not getting enough blood.
messages.What you can do: Rest when pain comes, take your medicines and avoid heavy exertion until reviewed.
messages.When to get help: Call emergency help for pain lasting over 15 minutes, with sweating, nausea or breathlessness.

messages.What it is: Cardiogenic shock is a critical condition where the heart cannot pump enough blood.
messages.What you can do: Follow your hospital team's advice closely after discharge.
messages.When to get help: This is a hospital emergency - call for help at once for collapse or severe breathlessness.

messages.What it is: Cardiomyopathy is a disease of the heart muscle that weakens its pumping. Treatment helps.
messages.What you can do: Take medicines daily, avoid alcohol, limit salt and attend all heart checks.
messages.When to get help: Get help for breathlessness, swelling, palpitations or fainting.

messages.What it is: You have disease of the heart or blood vessels. Medicines and lifestyle reduce further events.
messages.What you can do: Take your tablets daily, stop smoking, keep pressure and cholesterol controlled and stay active.
messages.When to get help: Get urgent help for chest pain, breathlessness, weakness or slurred speech.

messages.What it is: A bulge in the neck artery that needs monitoring by a specialist.
messages.What you can do: Control blood pressure, stop smoking and attend all vascular follow-up.
messages.When to get help: Get urgent help for sudden weakness, slurred speech or a swelling in the neck that grows.

messages.What it is: A clot has travelled in the neck artery. Treatment now aims to prevent a stroke.
messages.What you can do: Take blood thinners and statin as prescribed, never miss doses, and attend follow-up.
messages.When to get help: Call emergency help for face droop, arm weakness or slurred speech.

messages.What it is: The artery to your brain is narrowed. Medicines or surgery reduce stroke risk.
messages.What you can do: Take antiplatelet and statin daily, control pressure and sugar, stop smoking.
messages.When to get help: Call emergency help for weakness, slurred speech or sudden vision loss.

messages.What it is: A clot in the neck artery raises stroke risk. Treatment reduces that risk.
messages.What you can do: Take blood thinners and statin daily, control pressure and stop smoking.
messages.When to get help: Call emergency help for weakness, numbness, slurred speech or vision loss.

messages.What it is: A bruit is a sound over the neck artery that may mean narrowing. Tests will check this.
messages.What you can do: Control pressure and cholesterol, stop smoking and take aspirin or statin if prescribed.
messages.When to get help: Get urgent help for weakness, slurred speech or vision loss - these may be stroke signs.

messages.What it is: Fat around the waist raises diabetes and heart risk more than fat elsewhere.
messages.What you can do: Reduce rice and sugar, walk daily and aim for a waist under 90 cm (men) or 80 cm (women).
messages.When to get help: Ask for a sugar and cholesterol test if you have not had one this year.

messages.What it is: Chest pain has many causes, but it should never be ignored if it comes from the heart.
messages.What you can do: Note when it occurs, what brings it on and what relieves it, and tell your doctor.
messages.When to get help: Call for help now if pain is crushing, spreads to arm or jaw, or comes with sweating.

messages.What it is: Yellow patches on the eyelids are cholesterol deposits and may signal high blood cholesterol.
messages.What you can do: Ask for a cholesterol test. Cut oily and fried food and stay active.
messages.When to get help: See a doctor to check your cholesterol and heart risk.

messages.What it is: Your heart muscle has a long-term reduced blood supply. Treatment protects it and prevents attacks.
messages.What you can do: Never miss your heart tablets, keep active within your limits and eat less oil and salt.
messages.When to get help: Get urgent help for new or worsening chest pain, or pain at rest.

messages.What it is: Your kidneys work less well than they should. Good pressure and sugar control slows this.
messages.What you can do: Take your tablets, keep pressure below 130/80, avoid painkillers like ibuprofen and limit salt.
messages.When to get help: See a doctor for swelling, reduced urine, breathlessness or severe tiredness.

messages.What it is: Your kidneys have nearly stopped working. Dialysis or transplant planning keeps you well.
messages.What you can do: Follow your fluid and diet plan closely, take medicines and attend every dialysis session.
messages.When to get help: Seek urgent help for breathlessness, chest pain, confusion or missed dialysis.

messages.What it is: Stage 1 kidney disease means early signs of damage but normal function. Protect your kidneys now.
messages.What you can do: Control blood pressure and sugar, avoid anti-inflammatory painkillers and stop smoking.
messages.When to get help: See a doctor for foamy urine, swelling or high pressure readings.

messages.What it is: Stage 2 kidney disease means mildly reduced function. Protecting your kidneys now prevents decline.
messages.What you can do: Keep pressure below 130/80, control sugar, avoid ibuprofen-type painkillers and limit salt.
messages.When to get help: See a doctor for swelling, reduced urine or rising pressure.

messages.What it is: Stage 3 means your kidneys work at about half strength. Treatment can slow further loss.
messages.What you can do: Take pressure tablets daily, avoid ibuprofen-type painkillers, limit salt, check bloods 6-monthly.
messages.When to get help: See a doctor for swelling, breathlessness, itching or reduced urine.

messages.What it is: Stage 3A means moderately reduced kidney function. Good control slows further loss.
messages.What you can do: Keep pressure below 130/80, control sugar, avoid ibuprofen-type painkillers, check bloods 6-monthly.
messages.When to get help: See a doctor for swelling, breathlessness or reduced urine.

messages.What it is: Stage 3B means kidney function is reduced to around a third. Careful control matters.
messages.What you can do: Take tablets daily, avoid anti-inflammatory painkillers, limit salt and attend kidney reviews.
messages.When to get help: See a doctor for swelling, breathlessness, itching or nausea.

messages.What it is: Stage 4 means your kidneys are severely reduced. Specialist care helps plan the next steps.
messages.What you can do: Attend kidney clinic, follow diet advice on salt, potassium and protein, and take tablets daily.
messages.When to get help: Seek help urgently for breathlessness, confusion, vomiting or very little urine.

messages.What it is: Your kidneys have nearly stopped working. Dialysis or transplant planning keeps you well.
messages.What you can do: Follow your fluid and diet plan closely, take medicines and attend every dialysis session.
messages.When to get help: Seek urgent help for breathlessness, chest pain, confusion or missed dialysis.

messages.What it is: Sudden confusion can be caused by infection, low sugar, dehydration or medicines.
messages.What you can do: A family member should check sugar if diabetic, give fluids and bring all medicines to the clinic.
messages.When to get help: Seek urgent help - sudden confusion always needs assessment.

messages.What it is: The arteries supplying your heart are narrowed. Medicines and lifestyle reduce heart attack risk.
messages.What you can do: Take aspirin, statin and pressure tablets daily. Stop smoking and walk regularly.
messages.When to get help: Call for help at once for chest pain over 15 minutes, especially with sweating or breathlessness.

messages.What it is: Most coughs settle within 3 weeks. A cough lasting longer needs checking.
messages.What you can do: Drink warm fluids, avoid smoke and dust, and rest.
messages.When to get help: See a doctor for cough over 3 weeks, blood in phlegm, fever, weight loss or breathlessness.

messages.What it is: A DVT is a clot in a deep leg vein. Blood thinners stop it growing or travelling to the lungs.
messages.What you can do: Take your blood thinner exactly as prescribed, stay active and keep hydrated.
messages.When to get help: Call emergency help for sudden breathlessness, chest pain or coughing blood.

messages.What it is: Dehydration means your body lacks fluid. It strains the kidneys and can lower blood pressure.
messages.What you can do: Drink water or oral rehydration solution steadily, and rest in the shade.
messages.When to get help: Seek help if you feel dizzy, confused, pass very little urine or cannot keep fluids down.

messages.What it is: Delusional disorder causes fixed beliefs that others do not share. Treatment helps.
messages.What you can do: Take medicines as prescribed and keep appointments.
messages.When to get help: Contact your clinic if distress increases or you feel unsafe.

messages.What it is: Strong beliefs that others do not share can be part of an illness that treatment can help.
messages.What you can do: Take medicines as prescribed and keep appointments.
messages.When to get help: Contact your clinic if distress increases or you feel unsafe.

messages.What it is: Depression is a common illness affecting mood, sleep and energy. Treatment works for most people.
messages.What you can do: Take medicines as prescribed, keep a daily routine, stay active and connect with people.
messages.When to get help: If you have thoughts of harming yourself, call 1926 (NIMH) or Sumithrayo 011 2696666 now.

sourceNames: Depressive disorder due to another medical condition with depressive features

messages.What it is: Long-term illness often brings low mood. Treating both together improves each.
messages.What you can do: Stay active within your limits, keep social contact and take medicines as prescribed.
messages.When to get help: Contact your clinic if mood worsens. Call 1926 for thoughts of self-harm.

sourceNames: Major depressive disorder, single episode with atypical features

messages.What it is: Your depression causes more sleep and appetite than usual. It responds well to treatment.
messages.What you can do: Take medicines daily, keep regular waking times and stay active.
messages.When to get help: Contact your clinic if worsening. Call 1926 for thoughts of self-harm.

messages.What it is: Depression is a common illness affecting mood, sleep and energy. Treatment works for most people.
messages.What you can do: Take medicines as prescribed, keep a daily routine, stay active and connect with people.
messages.When to get help: If you have thoughts of harming yourself, call 1926 (NIMH) or Sumithrayo 011 2696666 now.

messages.What it is: Diabetes means your blood sugar is too high. Good control protects your eyes, kidneys and heart.
messages.What you can do: Take your medicines daily, eat less sugar and rice, walk 30 minutes a day and check HbA1c 3-monthly.
messages.When to get help: See a doctor soon for very high sugars, vomiting, drowsiness, or a foot wound that will not heal.

messages.What it is: Diabetes in pregnancy needs close control to protect your baby's growth and your own health.
messages.What you can do: Attend every antenatal visit, take insulin or tablets as prescribed and check sugars daily.
messages.When to get help: Get urgent help for very high or very low sugars, reduced baby movements or severe headache.

sourceNames: Type II diabetes mellitus with peripheral circulatory disorder

messages.What it is: Diabetes has narrowed the blood vessels in your legs. This slows healing and can cause pain.
messages.What you can do: Stop smoking, walk daily, control sugar and check your feet every day for cuts or colour change.
messages.When to get help: Seek urgent help for a cold, pale or painful foot, or a wound that is not healing.

messages.What it is: High sugar has affected the small blood vessels at the back of your eye. Treatment protects sight.
messages.What you can do: Keep sugar and blood pressure well controlled and attend every eye check, even if vision seems fine.
messages.When to get help: See an eye doctor urgently for sudden blurring, floaters, dark patches or loss of vision.

messages.What it is: A foot ulcer in diabetes heals slowly and can become infected. Careful daily care is vital.
messages.What you can do: Check both feet daily, keep the wound clean and covered, and never walk barefoot.
messages.When to get help: Go to the clinic at once if the wound smells, spreads, turns black or you have fever.

sourceNames: Type II (Non-Insulin Dependent Type) or Unspecified Type Diabetes Mellitus with ketoacidosis, not stated as uncontrolled

messages.What it is: Ketoacidosis is a dangerous state where very high sugar makes acid build up in the blood.
messages.What you can do: Never stop insulin, even when unwell. Drink water and check sugars more often when sick.
messages.When to get help: Go to hospital at once if vomiting, tummy pain, fast breathing or fruity-smelling breath.

messages.What it is: Diarrhoea is usually from infection and settles in a few days. Fluids are the main treatment.
messages.What you can do: Drink oral rehydration solution after each loose stool, wash hands, and eat light meals.
messages.When to get help: Seek help if it lasts over 3 days, there is blood, high fever, or you cannot keep fluids down.

messages.What it is: Difficulty breathing can come from the lungs, heart or anaemia and needs assessment.
messages.What you can do: Sit upright, stay calm and use your inhaler if you have one.
messages.When to get help: Seek urgent help if breathless at rest, with chest pain, or if lips turn blue.

messages.What it is: Difficulty passing urine can come from prostate, bladder or nerve problems.
messages.What you can do: Do not hold urine for long periods, limit evening fluids and cut caffeine.
messages.When to get help: Seek urgent help if you cannot pass urine at all or have pain and a swollen tummy.

messages.What it is: You are allergic to a medicine. Every clinic and pharmacy must know this.
messages.What you can do: Carry a note of the drug name and show it whenever you are given a prescription.
messages.When to get help: Seek urgent help for lip swelling, breathing difficulty or widespread rash after any medicine.

messages.What it is: Two of your medicines can interact. Your doctor will adjust them.
messages.What you can do: Take a full list of your medicines to every visit, including any bought over the counter.
messages.When to get help: Contact your clinic if you notice new symptoms after a change of medicine.

messages.What it is: Some medicines, like steroids, raise blood sugar. Your doctor will balance this with your needs.
messages.What you can do: Do not stop the medicine that caused it without advice. Limit sugar and stay active.
messages.When to get help: See your doctor if sugars stay high or if you feel very thirsty or drowsy.

messages.What it is: Some medicines can lower mood. Your doctor can review and adjust them.
messages.What you can do: Do not stop any medicine on your own - tell your doctor which one you think is responsible.
messages.When to get help: Contact your clinic soon. Call 1926 if you have thoughts of self-harm.

messages.What it is: Some medicines affect sexual function. This is common and can often be adjusted.
messages.What you can do: Do not stop the medicine on your own - discuss options with your doctor.
messages.When to get help: Ask at your next appointment; alternatives are usually available.

messages.What it is: A dry cough can be from a virus, asthma, reflux or blood-pressure tablets (ACE inhibitors).
messages.What you can do: Sip warm water and avoid smoke. Tell your doctor if it began after starting a new tablet.
messages.When to get help: See a doctor if it lasts over 3 weeks or comes with breathlessness or weight loss.

sourceNames: Erectile dysfunction associated with type 2 diabetes mellitus

messages.What it is: Diabetes can affect nerves and blood flow, making erections difficult. This is common and treatable.
messages.What you can do: Good sugar and blood pressure control help. Stop smoking and limit alcohol.
messages.When to get help: Talk to your doctor - safe treatments are available and it can be a sign of heart risk.

messages.What it is: Essential hypertension is high blood pressure with no single cause. It is lifelong but controllable.
messages.What you can do: Tablets work only if taken every day. Cut salt, limit alcohol and keep active.
messages.When to get help: Seek help for readings over 180/110, severe headache or chest pain.

messages.What it is: Well done for stopping smoking. Your heart and lung risk falls every year you stay smoke-free.
messages.What you can do: Avoid places and situations that tempt you, and remind yourself why you stopped.
messages.When to get help: If you relapse, ask your clinic for help - most people need several attempts.

messages.What it is: Heart disease runs in your family, so your own risk is higher. Prevention works.
messages.What you can do: Check blood pressure, sugar and cholesterol yearly, stop smoking and walk daily.
messages.When to get help: See a doctor if you have chest pain on exertion.

messages.What it is: Diabetes runs in your family, which raises your own risk. Early action can prevent it.
messages.What you can do: Keep a healthy weight, walk daily, cut sugary drinks and have a sugar test every year.
messages.When to get help: Ask for a test if you have thirst, frequent urination or slow-healing wounds.

patientFacingName: Family history of early heart disease
sourceNames: Family history of premature coronary heart disease

messages.What it is: A close relative had heart disease young, so your risk is raised. Early checks can protect you.
messages.What you can do: Ask for cholesterol, sugar and pressure tests, stop smoking and stay active.
messages.When to get help: See a doctor for chest pain, especially on exertion.

messages.What it is: High blood pressure runs in your family, so your own risk is higher.
messages.What you can do: Check your pressure yearly, keep salt low, stay active and keep a healthy weight.
messages.When to get help: See a doctor if readings are above 140/90.

messages.What it is: Fast breathing can be from infection, asthma, heart problems or very high sugar.
messages.What you can do: Rest, stay upright and use inhalers if prescribed.
messages.When to get help: Seek urgent help if breathing stays fast at rest, or with fever, chest pain or drowsiness.

messages.What it is: A fast heart rate can come from fever, anxiety, anaemia, thyroid or heart problems.
messages.What you can do: Rest, drink fluids and avoid caffeine. Note your pulse when it happens.
messages.When to get help: Get help if it is over 120 at rest, or with chest pain, fainting or breathlessness.

messages.What it is: Fever is the body fighting infection. Most fevers settle in a few days.
messages.What you can do: Rest, drink plenty of fluids and take paracetamol. Avoid aspirin in children.
messages.When to get help: See a doctor if fever lasts over 3 days, or with rash, bleeding, breathing difficulty or drowsiness.

messages.What it is: Swollen legs from the heart mean fluid is building up. Water tablets and salt limits help.
messages.What you can do: Take water tablets in the morning, raise your legs when resting and limit salt.
messages.When to get help: See a doctor if swelling worsens, or urgently if you become breathless.

messages.What it is: You react to a particular food. Careful avoidance prevents reactions.
messages.What you can do: Check ingredients, tell hosts and restaurants, and carry any prescribed emergency medicine.
messages.When to get help: Seek urgent help for lip or throat swelling, wheeze or fainting after eating.

messages.What it is: Frozen shoulder is a stiff painful shoulder, more common with diabetes. It recovers slowly.
messages.What you can do: Do daily stretching exercises, use heat and paracetamol, and keep sugar well controlled.
messages.When to get help: See a doctor if pain stops sleep or if the arm becomes weak.

messages.What it is: Generalised anxiety is constant worry about many things. Treatment helps you regain control.
messages.What you can do: Take medicines as prescribed, limit caffeine, exercise daily and try relaxation exercises.
messages.When to get help: Contact your clinic if worsening. Call 1926 if in crisis.

messages.What it is: Swelling all over can come from the heart, kidneys or liver, and needs tests.
messages.What you can do: Limit salt, raise your legs when sitting and note any change in urine or breathing.
messages.When to get help: Seek help urgently if breathless, or if swelling is rapid or involves the face.

messages.What it is: Gestational diabetes is high sugar in pregnancy. Controlling it keeps you and your baby safe.
messages.What you can do: Eat small regular meals, limit sweets and rice, walk daily and check sugars as advised.
messages.When to get help: Contact your clinic if sugars stay high, or if you feel unwell. Test again 6 weeks after birth.

messages.What it is: A goitre is an enlarged thyroid gland. Most are harmless, but tests check its function.
messages.What you can do: Use iodised salt and attend for thyroid blood tests and any scans advised.
messages.When to get help: See a doctor if the swelling grows quickly or causes difficulty swallowing or breathing.

messages.What it is: Most headaches are tension-type or migraine. High blood pressure rarely causes them.
messages.What you can do: Rest, drink water, limit screen time and use paracetamol. Note any triggers.
messages.When to get help: Seek urgent help for a sudden severe headache, with fever and stiff neck, or weakness.

messages.What it is: You have had a heart attack. Your tablets now protect your heart and prevent another one.
messages.What you can do: Take aspirin, statin, beta blocker and ACE inhibitor daily. Stop smoking and attend rehab.
messages.When to get help: Call emergency services for chest pain, breathlessness or collapse.

messages.What it is: Your heart has been affected by another condition. Close follow-up protects it.
messages.What you can do: Take all medicines and attend your heart appointments.
messages.When to get help: Get help for chest pain, breathlessness, swelling or palpitations.

messages.What it is: You have a heart condition. Regular medicines and follow-up keep it stable.
messages.What you can do: Take tablets daily, limit salt and fat, stop smoking and keep gently active.
messages.When to get help: Get urgent help for chest pain, breathlessness or fainting.

messages.What it is: Heart failure means your heart pumps less strongly. Medicines help it work better and ease tiredness
messages.What you can do: Take tablets daily, weigh yourself each morning, limit salt and fluids as advised.
messages.When to get help: Get help if weight rises 2 kg in 3 days, ankles swell or you cannot lie flat without breathlessness.

messages.What it is: Your symptoms may be coming from the heart, so tests are needed to be sure.
messages.What you can do: Avoid heavy exertion until reviewed and note what brings symptoms on.
messages.When to get help: Call for help at once for chest pain, fainting or sudden breathlessness.

messages.What it is: Heartburn is a burning feeling from stomach acid. It usually settles with diet changes.
messages.What you can do: Eat smaller meals, avoid spicy and oily food, and do not lie down straight after eating.
messages.When to get help: See a doctor if it lasts over 2 weeks, or with swallowing difficulty or weight loss.

messages.What it is: High blood pressure rarely causes symptoms but silently damages the heart, brain and kidneys.
messages.What you can do: Take tablets daily, use less salt, walk 30 minutes a day and check your pressure regularly.
messages.When to get help: Get urgent help for severe headache, chest pain, weakness on one side or blurred vision.

sourceNames: Hypertension complicating pregnancy, childbirth, or the puerperium

messages.What it is: High blood pressure in pregnancy needs close monitoring to protect you and your baby.
messages.What you can do: Attend every antenatal visit, take prescribed tablets and rest when advised.
messages.When to get help: Get urgent help for severe headache, vision changes, tummy pain or sudden swelling.

messages.What it is: Your blood sugar is higher than it should be. Over time this can harm eyes, kidneys and nerves.
messages.What you can do: Take your medicines, avoid sweets and sugary drinks, and eat smaller portions of rice.
messages.When to get help: Seek help today if you are very thirsty, drowsy, vomiting or breathing fast.

messages.What it is: High cholesterol builds fatty deposits in arteries. Lowering it prevents heart attack and stroke.
messages.What you can do: Take your statin daily, use less coconut oil and fried food, eat more vegetables and walk daily.
messages.When to get help: Ask for a repeat cholesterol test in 3 months and a review if you get muscle pain on statins.

messages.What it is: You have had allergies before. Keep a record so new medicines can be chosen safely.
messages.What you can do: Tell every clinic which drugs or foods caused problems.
messages.When to get help: Seek urgent help for any swelling of the face or breathing difficulty.

messages.What it is: You have had high cholesterol before. It often returns without ongoing care.
messages.What you can do: Keep to a low-oil diet, stay active and check cholesterol yearly.
messages.When to get help: See a doctor if cholesterol rises again or you develop chest pain.

messages.What it is: You have had diabetes in the past. It can return, so regular checks are important.
messages.What you can do: Keep a healthy weight, stay active and have a sugar test at least once a year.
messages.When to get help: See a doctor if you notice thirst, frequent urination or tiredness.

messages.What it is: You have had high blood pressure before. It can return, so keep checking.
messages.What you can do: Check your pressure every 3-6 months, keep salt low and stay active.
messages.When to get help: See a doctor if readings go above 140/90.

messages.What it is: A hypertensive crisis is dangerously high pressure that can damage organs within hours.
messages.What you can do: Take your medicines exactly as prescribed and attend all follow-up visits.
messages.When to get help: Go to hospital now if pressure is above 180/120 with headache, chest pain or confusion.

messages.What it is: You have a blood pressure condition. Keeping it controlled prevents stroke and heart disease.
messages.What you can do: Take medicines daily, reduce salt and check your pressure at home if you can.
messages.When to get help: Get help urgently for chest pain, severe headache or weakness in the face or limbs.

messages.What it is: High blood pressure has affected the blood vessels in your eyes. Control prevents further damage.
messages.What you can do: Keep pressure under 140/90, take tablets daily and attend eye checks.
messages.When to get help: See a doctor urgently for sudden blurring or loss of vision.

messages.What it is: Years of high pressure have made your heart work harder and thicken. Control protects it.
messages.What you can do: Take tablets daily, cut salt, stay active and keep a healthy weight.
messages.When to get help: Get help for breathlessness, chest pain, swollen ankles or palpitations.

messages.What it is: High blood pressure has affected your kidneys. Good control slows further damage.
messages.What you can do: Keep pressure below 130/80, take medicines daily, avoid painkillers like ibuprofen and limit salt.
messages.When to get help: See a doctor for swollen legs, foamy urine or reduced urine.

messages.What it is: Poor sleep worsens blood pressure, sugar and mood. Good sleep habits often help.
messages.What you can do: Keep fixed sleep times, avoid screens and caffeine in the evening and keep the bedroom dark.
messages.When to get help: Talk to your clinic if poor sleep lasts over a month or affects daily life.

messages.What it is: Your anaemia is from low iron. Iron tablets and iron-rich food restore your levels.
messages.What you can do: Take iron with vitamin C (a fruit), not with tea. Eat greens, lentils, meat and eggs.
messages.When to get help: See a doctor if you have black stools, heavy periods or no improvement after 3 months.

messages.What it is: An arrhythmia is an abnormal heart rhythm. Many are harmless; some need treatment.
messages.What you can do: Take any prescribed tablets, limit caffeine and alcohol, and note when symptoms happen.
messages.When to get help: Get urgent help for fainting, chest pain or a very fast heartbeat that does not settle.

messages.What it is: Itching can come from dry skin, allergy, kidney or liver problems, or high sugar.
messages.What you can do: Moisturise, use mild soap, keep cool and take antihistamines if advised.
messages.When to get help: See a doctor if it lasts over 2 weeks, is all over, or comes with yellow skin or eyes.

messages.What it is: A stone in the kidney or tube can cause severe pain. Most pass with fluids and pain relief.
messages.What you can do: Drink 2-3 litres of water daily, reduce salt and follow diet advice to prevent new stones.
messages.When to get help: Seek urgent help for severe pain with fever, vomiting or inability to pass urine.

messages.What it is: A kidney stone forms from minerals in urine. Plenty of water helps prevent more.
messages.What you can do: Drink 2-3 litres of water daily and limit salt and excess meat.
messages.When to get help: Seek urgent help for severe pain with fever, vomiting or no urine.

messages.What it is: Leg pain on walking means narrowed leg arteries. Walking actually helps them improve.
messages.What you can do: Walk daily to the point of pain, rest, then continue. Stop smoking and take statin and aspirin.
messages.When to get help: Get urgent help for a cold, pale or numb foot, or pain at rest.

messages.What it is: Small daily habits - food, movement, sleep and no tobacco - do more for health than any tablet.
messages.What you can do: Walk 30 minutes a day, fill half your plate with vegetables, sleep 7 hours and avoid tobacco.
messages.When to get help: Ask your clinic for a yearly check of pressure, sugar and cholesterol.

messages.What it is: A medicine has affected your liver. Stopping it usually allows recovery.
messages.What you can do: Do not take the medicine again. Avoid alcohol and paracetamol overuse.
messages.When to get help: Seek help for yellow eyes, dark urine, severe tummy pain or vomiting.

messages.What it is: Long-standing low mood is treatable. Small steady changes and treatment help.
messages.What you can do: Keep a routine, exercise daily, limit alcohol and take medicines as prescribed.
messages.When to get help: Contact your clinic if mood drops further. Call 1926 for thoughts of self-harm.

messages.What it is: Loss of appetite can follow illness, medicines or low mood. It needs checking if it persists.
messages.What you can do: Eat small frequent meals and keep drinking fluids.
messages.When to get help: See a doctor if it lasts over 2 weeks or you are losing weight.

messages.What it is: Low calcium can cause cramps and tingling. Diet and supplements correct it.
messages.What you can do: Eat milk, yoghurt, small fish with bones and green leaves. Take supplements if prescribed.
messages.When to get help: Seek help for muscle spasms, tingling around the mouth or fits.

messages.What it is: Menopause is a natural change. Heart and bone risks rise afterwards, so prevention matters.
messages.What you can do: Stay active, eat calcium-rich foods and check pressure and cholesterol yearly.
messages.When to get help: Talk to your clinic about hot flushes, mood or bleeding after periods have stopped.

messages.What it is: Your haemoglobin is slightly low. Diet changes and finding the cause usually fix it.
messages.What you can do: Eat iron-rich foods and take any iron tablets prescribed. Recheck in 3 months.
messages.When to get help: See a doctor if you feel breathless or notice black stools or heavy bleeding.

messages.What it is: Mild depression often improves with routine, activity, sleep and talking therapy.
messages.What you can do: Walk daily, keep regular sleep, limit alcohol and talk to someone you trust.
messages.When to get help: See your clinic if it lasts over 2 weeks or worsens. Call 1926 if you have thoughts of self-harm.

messages.What it is: Mild depression often improves with routine, activity, sleep and talking therapy.
messages.What you can do: Walk daily, keep regular sleep, limit alcohol and talk to someone you trust.
messages.When to get help: See your clinic if it lasts over 2 weeks or worsens. Call 1926 if you have thoughts of self-harm.

messages.What it is: Your blood pressure is mildly high. Tablets and lifestyle changes together control it best.
messages.What you can do: Take your medicine every day, cut salt and stay active. Check pressure monthly.
messages.When to get help: Get help if readings go above 160/100 or you have headaches or chest pain.

messages.What it is: Your haemoglobin is moderately low. Treatment and finding the cause are important.
messages.What you can do: Take iron or other tablets as prescribed, eat iron-rich foods and rest when tired.
messages.When to get help: See a doctor soon for breathlessness, chest pain, dizziness or bleeding.

messages.What it is: Moderate dehydration needs prompt fluids to protect your kidneys and blood pressure.
messages.What you can do: Drink oral rehydration solution in small frequent sips, and rest.
messages.When to get help: Seek help today if you cannot keep fluids down, are dizzy or pass very little urine.

messages.What it is: Moderate depression affects daily life. Medicines and talking therapy together work best.
messages.What you can do: Take antidepressants daily - they take 2-4 weeks to work. Keep a routine and stay active.
messages.When to get help: Contact your clinic if worsening. Call 1926 or Sumithrayo 011 2696666 for thoughts of self-harm.

messages.What it is: Moderate depression affects daily life. Medicines and talking therapy together work best.
messages.What you can do: Take antidepressants daily - they take 2-4 weeks to work. Keep a routine and stay active.
messages.When to get help: Contact your clinic if worsening. Call 1926 or Sumithrayo 011 2696666 for thoughts of self-harm.

messages.What it is: Your blood pressure is moderately high, so the risk of stroke and heart attack is raised.
messages.What you can do: Take all tablets daily, never skip doses, and reduce salt. You may need more than one medicine.
messages.When to get help: Get urgent help for readings above 180/110, severe headache, chest pain or weakness.

messages.What it is: Muscle and joint pain is common. Movement, heat and simple painkillers usually help.
messages.What you can do: Stay gently active, use warm compresses and paracetamol first. Avoid long courses of ibuprofen.
messages.When to get help: See a doctor for a hot, swollen joint, fever, or pain that wakes you at night.

messages.What it is: You have had a type of heart attack. Medicines and lifestyle changes reduce the risk of another.
messages.What you can do: Take antiplatelets, statin and pressure tablets daily. Stop smoking and attend follow-up.
messages.When to get help: Call emergency help for chest pain, breathlessness or fainting.

messages.What it is: Extra weight raises the risk of diabetes, high pressure and joint problems. Small changes help.
messages.What you can do: Aim to lose 5% of your weight: smaller rice portions, no sugary drinks and 30 minutes walking daily.
messages.When to get help: Ask for a sugar, pressure and cholesterol check if you have not had one this year.

messages.What it is: OCD causes unwanted thoughts and repeated actions. Treatment reduces both.
messages.What you can do: Take medicines as prescribed and practise the exercises your therapist gives you.
messages.When to get help: Contact your clinic if worsening. Call 1926 if in crisis.

messages.What it is: Strong need for order and control can cause stress. Therapy helps balance this.
messages.What you can do: Notice when perfectionism causes distress and practise letting small things go.
messages.When to get help: Contact your clinic if it affects relationships or work.

messages.What it is: Your thyroid makes too much hormone, causing weight loss, sweating and a fast heart. It is treatable
messages.What you can do: Take your tablets daily, avoid excess caffeine and have regular blood tests.
messages.When to get help: Seek help for a very fast heartbeat, fever, confusion or a sore throat while on carbimazole.

messages.What it is: Burning when passing urine is usually a urine infection, which is easily treated.
messages.What you can do: Drink plenty of water and complete any antibiotic course.
messages.When to get help: See a doctor if there is fever, back pain, blood in urine, or if it lasts over 2 days.

messages.What it is: Palpitations are the feeling of your heart racing or skipping. Often harmless but worth checking.
messages.What you can do: Cut caffeine, alcohol and smoking. Note when they happen and how long they last.
messages.When to get help: Get help if they come with chest pain, fainting or breathlessness.

messages.What it is: A panic attack is sudden intense fear with a racing heart. It passes and is not dangerous.
messages.What you can do: Breathe slowly - in for 4, out for 6 - and remind yourself it will pass in minutes.
messages.When to get help: See your clinic if attacks are frequent. Get urgent help if chest pain does not settle.

messages.What it is: Large volumes of urine can mean high sugar, high calcium or a kidney problem.
messages.What you can do: Drink water to stay hydrated and note how much you are passing.
messages.When to get help: See a doctor soon for a sugar and kidney test.

messages.What it is: Passing very little urine can mean dehydration or a kidney problem.
messages.What you can do: Drink water steadily through the day and note how much urine you pass.
messages.When to get help: Seek help today if urine is very dark, very little, or you feel drowsy or swollen.

messages.What it is: Passing a lot of urine can be a sign of high blood sugar or a bladder problem.
messages.What you can do: Note how often you go and drink water, not sugary drinks, until you are checked.
messages.When to get help: See a doctor if it continues, or if you have thirst, burning or blood in urine.

messages.What it is: You have had a heart or blood vessel problem before, so prevention matters more than ever.
messages.What you can do: Keep taking preventive tablets, stop smoking, stay active and control pressure and cholesterol.
messages.When to get help: Get urgent help for chest pain, weakness or slurred speech.

messages.What it is: A peptic ulcer is a sore in the stomach lining, often from infection or painkillers.
messages.What you can do: Complete the full course of tablets, avoid ibuprofen-type painkillers, alcohol and smoking.
messages.When to get help: Seek urgent help for black stools, vomiting blood or severe sudden tummy pain.

messages.What it is: Your pressure is mildly raised. Lifestyle changes now can avoid the need for tablets later.
messages.What you can do: Halve your salt, lose extra weight, walk daily and limit alcohol. Recheck in 1-3 months.
messages.When to get help: See a doctor if readings rise above 140/90.

messages.What it is: Small amounts of protein in urine are an early warning of kidney strain, often from diabetes or BP.
messages.What you can do: ACE inhibitor or ARB tablets, tight sugar and pressure control, and no smoking protect the kidneys.
messages.When to get help: Ask for a repeat test in 3-6 months and see a doctor if swelling appears.

messages.What it is: A single high reading does not always mean hypertension, but it needs rechecking.
messages.What you can do: Rest 5 minutes before measuring, avoid coffee and smoking beforehand, and recheck within a week.
messages.When to get help: See a doctor if readings stay above 140/90, or urgently if above 180/110.

sourceNames: Recurrent depressive disorder, current episode mild

messages.What it is: Your depression has returned in a mild form. Early action helps prevent it deepening.
messages.What you can do: Restart the routines that helped before, stay active and take medicines as prescribed.
messages.When to get help: Contact your clinic if it worsens. Call 1926 if you have thoughts of self-harm.

messages.What it is: Your depression has returned. Restarting treatment early shortens the episode.
messages.What you can do: Take medicines daily, keep appointments and use the coping strategies that helped before.
messages.When to get help: Contact your clinic if worsening. Call 1926 or Sumithrayo 011 2696666 for thoughts of self-harm.

sourceNames: Recurrent depressive disorder, current episode severe without psychotic symptoms

messages.What it is: Your severe depression has returned. Prompt treatment and support help recovery.
messages.What you can do: Take medicines daily, keep every appointment and tell someone close how you feel.
messages.When to get help: If you have thoughts of ending your life, call 1926 or Sumithrayo 011 2696666 or go to hospital now.

sourceNames: Recurrent depressive disorder, current episode severe with psychotic symptoms
Severe recurrent major depression with psychotic features

messages.What it is: Severe depression can bring confusing thoughts or voices. Treatment helps these settle.
messages.What you can do: Take all medicines, keep appointments and let family support you.
messages.When to get help: Go to hospital or call 1926 now if you have thoughts of harming yourself or others.

messages.What it is: Your blood salts (sodium or potassium) are out of balance, often from medicines or dehydration.
messages.What you can do: Follow diet and fluid advice, and take or pause medicines exactly as told.
messages.When to get help: Seek help for confusion, weakness, palpitations or muscle cramps.

messages.What it is: Schizoaffective disorder affects mood and thinking. Medicines keep it stable.
messages.What you can do: Take medicines daily, keep regular sleep and attend all appointments.
messages.When to get help: Get urgent help if symptoms return or for thoughts of self-harm. Call 1926.

messages.What it is: Schizoaffective disorder affects mood and thinking. Medicines keep it stable.
messages.What you can do: Take medicines daily, keep regular sleep and attend all appointments.
messages.When to get help: Get urgent help if symptoms return or for thoughts of self-harm. Call 1926.

messages.What it is: Schizophrenia affects thinking and perception. Regular medicines keep symptoms controlled.
messages.What you can do: Take medicines every day even when well, keep appointments and avoid alcohol and drugs.
messages.When to get help: Get urgent help if voices or fears return, or for thoughts of harming yourself or others.

messages.What it is: Your high blood pressure has an underlying cause, such as a kidney or hormone problem.
messages.What you can do: Treat the cause and take your tablets. Keep salt low and attend all follow-up tests.
messages.When to get help: Seek help for very high readings, headaches, palpitations or sudden swelling.

messages.What it is: You are not alone. Help is available and treatment reduces these feelings.
messages.What you can do: Keep every appointment and let someone close know how you feel each day.
messages.When to get help: Call 1926 (NIMH) or Sumithrayo 011 2696666 now, or go to the nearest hospital.

sourceNames: Severe depressive episode without psychotic symptoms

messages.What it is: Severe depression is a serious illness. Regular treatment and close follow-up help you recover.
messages.What you can do: Take medicines every day, keep every appointment and let someone close know how you feel.
messages.When to get help: If you have thoughts of ending your life, call 1926 or Sumithrayo 011 2696666 or go to hospital now.

sourceNames: Severe depressive episode with psychotic symptoms

messages.What it is: Severe depression can bring confusing thoughts or voices. Treatment helps these settle.
messages.What you can do: Take all medicines, keep appointments and let family support you.
messages.When to get help: Go to hospital or call 1926 now if you have thoughts of harming yourself or others.

patientFacingName: Severe depression with psychosis, single episode
sourceNames: Major depressive disorder, single episode, severe with psychotic features

messages.What it is: Severe depression can bring confusing thoughts or voices. Treatment helps these settle.
messages.What you can do: Take all medicines, keep appointments and let family support you.
messages.When to get help: Go to hospital or call 1926 now if you have thoughts of harming yourself or others.

sourceNames: Major depressive disorder, single episode, severe without psychotic features

messages.What it is: Severe depression is a serious illness. Regular treatment and close follow-up help you recover.
messages.What you can do: Take medicines every day, keep every appointment and let someone close know how you feel.
messages.When to get help: If you have thoughts of ending your life, call 1926 or Sumithrayo 011 2696666 or go to hospital now.

messages.What it is: Your blood pressure is very high. Prompt treatment protects your heart, brain and kidneys.
messages.What you can do: Take every dose, attend follow-up within days, and avoid salt, smoking and stress.
messages.When to get help: Go to hospital now if you have chest pain, severe headache, confusion or breathlessness.

messages.What it is: Your severe depression has returned. Prompt treatment and support help recovery.
messages.What you can do: Take medicines daily, keep every appointment and tell someone close how you feel.
messages.When to get help: If you have thoughts of ending your life, call 1926 or Sumithrayo 011 2696666 or go to hospital now.

messages.What it is: Sexual difficulties are common and often linked to diabetes, blood pressure or medicines.
messages.What you can do: Control sugar and pressure, stop smoking, limit alcohol and stay active.
messages.When to get help: Talk to your doctor - treatments are available and it may signal heart risk.

messages.What it is: Shortness of breath can be from the heart, lungs, anaemia or anxiety.
messages.What you can do: Note when it happens and pace your activities. Use inhalers if prescribed.
messages.When to get help: Seek urgent help if breathless at rest, waking at night gasping, or with chest pain.

messages.What it is: Psychiatric medicines can cause side effects such as stiffness, weight gain or drowsiness.
messages.What you can do: Do not stop the medicine suddenly - tell your doctor so the dose or drug can be changed.
messages.When to get help: Seek urgent help for high fever with stiffness, or severe restlessness.

messages.What it is: Social anxiety is strong fear of being judged by others. Talking therapy helps a lot.
messages.What you can do: Practise small social steps, breathe slowly and take medicines if prescribed.
messages.When to get help: Contact your clinic if it stops you working or seeing people.

messages.What it is: Ongoing stress raises blood pressure and sugar and makes healthy habits harder.
messages.What you can do: Try daily walking, breathing exercises, regular sleep and talking to someone you trust.
messages.When to get help: Talk to your clinic if stress affects sleep, appetite or mood for more than 2 weeks.

messages.What it is: You are not alone. Thoughts of self-harm are a sign of pain that can be treated.
messages.What you can do: Tell someone you trust today and keep your appointments. Keep away from means of harming yourself.
messages.When to get help: Call 1926 (NIMH) or Sumithrayo 011 2696666 now, or go to the nearest hospital.

messages.What it is: Your thyroid gland is not working normally. Blood tests guide the right treatment.
messages.What you can do: Take tablets as prescribed and attend for thyroid blood tests.
messages.When to get help: See a doctor for palpitations, marked weight change or a neck swelling.

messages.What it is: Tiredness can come from anaemia, thyroid, diabetes, poor sleep or low mood.
messages.What you can do: Keep regular sleep, eat iron-rich foods and stay gently active. Note any other symptoms.
messages.When to get help: See a doctor if it lasts over 2 weeks or comes with breathlessness, weight loss or low mood.

messages.What it is: Type 1 diabetes: your body makes no insulin, so insulin injections are essential every day.
messages.What you can do: Never miss insulin. Check sugars, carry glucose sweets and eat regular meals.
messages.When to get help: Urgent care if vomiting, tummy pain, fast breathing or sugar over 300 - this could be ketoacidosis.

messages.What it is: Type 2 diabetes: your body does not use insulin well, so sugar builds up in the blood.
messages.What you can do: Medicines, smaller rice portions, more vegetables and daily walking all lower your sugar.
messages.When to get help: Get help if you feel very thirsty, pass urine often, feel drowsy or have a wound that will not heal.

messages.What it is: Your thyroid makes too little hormone, causing tiredness, weight gain and feeling cold. Tablets help
messages.What you can do: Take levothyroxine every morning on an empty stomach and have blood tests as advised.
messages.When to get help: See a doctor if very tired, gaining weight or if you become pregnant - the dose may need changing.

messages.What it is: Your heart failure has flared up. Adjusting medicines and fluids will help you recover.
messages.What you can do: Take water tablets as prescribed, limit salt and fluid, and weigh yourself daily.
messages.When to get help: Get urgent help for breathlessness at rest, chest pain or fainting.
